title: Idempotent Tool Transcript Protocol and SDK Facades (TS/Py/Go)
creator: Amira Shah
description: Problem: Customers and SDKs need a safe, cross-language pattern for invoking external tools (function calls) while streaming incremental model output. Current SDK approaches either: 1) rely on best-effort deduplication at the server, or 2) accept duplicate side effects when a streaming connection is retried. This ticket designs and implements a transcript-based, idempotent protocol plus small client facades for TypeScript, Python, and Go to make resumable streaming tool invocations reliable and ergonomic.
rationale: High-level language clients must be able to: (a) resume a partially-completed streaming generation without re-triggering tool side effects, (b) reattach to an in-flight session and receive the same structured output frames, and (c) interoperate between older SDKs that don't support the full protocol. This reduces customer incidents and user friction for production workloads that call external systems (databases, webhooks, APIs) during generation.
proposed_solution: Introduce a lightweight 'transcript' envelope that annotates each tool invocation and streamed frame with a stable invocation_id, a monotonic sequence number, and a checksum of the tool input. Server-side will persist minimal transcript state for the lifetime of the session and accept idempotency keys for terminal tool result commits. SDKs will provide a small facade: startInvocation(...)->InvocationHandle, InvocationHandle.stream(handler) and InvocationHandle.resume(checkpoint). The facade will handle backpressure, checkpointing to disk (optional), and transparent retry semantics. For compatibility, the server accepts legacy frames and maps them to the transcript when possible, or falls back to best-effort deduplication with warnings in logs.
api_surface_examples: TypeScript example: const inv = client.invocations.start({tool:'http_post', body, idempotency_key}); await inv.stream(event => { if (event.type==='tool_call') handleToolCall(event); }); inv.checkpoint() -> {sessionId, seq} to persist

Python example: with client.invocations.start(...) as inv: for frame in inv.stream(): if frame['call']:
  reply = client.tools.exec(frame['call'], idempotency=frame['id']); inv.commit_tool_result(frame['seq'], reply)

Go example: h, _ := client.Invocations.Start(ctx, req); ch := h.Stream(ctx); for e := range ch { switch e.Kind { case ToolCall: go processTool(e) } }
  Resume: h.Resume(ctx, checkpoint) returns missing frames since checkpoint.seq
migration_notes:
- Server: add optional transcript persistence (TTL 24h default) and idempotency window for tool commit dedup (configurable per-project).
- SDKs: publish new minor versions with facades.
- Backwards compatibility: when Transcript headers are absent, server marks invocation as legacy and applies best-effort rules; SDK will surface a warning and suggest upgrade.
- Docs: add a migration guide and examples showing common patterns (webhook side effects, DB updates, long running tool calls).
acceptance_criteria: Server accepts and persists transcript envelopes and honors idempotency keys for tool commits
TS/Py/Go SDKs expose the InvocationHandle API and stream/resume behavior documented above
E2E test: simulate network interruption mid-tool-call; resumed client does not trigger duplicate external side effects (verified by test harness)
Compatibility test: older SDK clients still function and are marked as legacy in server logs without breaking live sessions
Documentation + migration guide published and linked from SDK release notes

Py SDK: implement context-manager friendly facade and example notebooks
